pr.title: gh-132399: ensure correct alignment of `PyInterpreterState` when UBSan is on
pr.body:
With that PR, the test suite passes for the free-threaded build with UBSan:

```sh
./configure --with-undefined-behavior-sanitizer --with-pydebug --prefix="$(pwd)/build" CC=clang LD=clang CFLAGS="-fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover"  LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover" -q --disable-gil
./python -m test -j0
```

There is still one UB failure (fixed by #131605) but this is not specific to free-threading.

cc @colesbury

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-132399 -->
* Issue: gh-132399
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -569,11 +569,28 @@ _PyInterpreterState_Enable(_PyRuntimeState *runtime)
     return _PyStatus_OK();
 }
 
+#ifdef _Py_HAS_UNDEFINED_BEHAVIOR_SANITIZER
+#define RAW_ALIGN_PTR_OFFSET sizeof(void *)
+#endif
 
-static PyInterpreterState *
+static inline PyInterpreterState *
review_comments.body: I don't think there's any reason to add `inline` to a `static` functions in a `.c` file like this

I think this will be safer and easier to understand if you make this a proper field in `PyInterpreterState`. The field can either store the original allocation pointer or an offset (possibly as a `uint8_t`).

review_comments.body:
I think that if we are going to include this code path, we should just perform the alignment unconditionally: 

* It's better to have our UBSan and other builds be as close as possible
* The extra space and checks are not a big deal in this case

review_comments.body: I'm ok with an unconditional custom alignment. Considering the size of an interpreter's size, it also makes sense to ease our life (I think the interpreter's size is about 40k or something along the lines, so adding a field shouldn't change much).

review_comments.body:
`void *` ? We don't need to treat `_malloced` as an integer anywhere.

We should also move the field farther down in the `_is` struct. It doesn't matter exactly where. There's a comment immediately below this about how `struct _ceval_state ceval` should be at the beginning.

I.. read the comment about the *last* field but I missed the one for the beginning! I think I wanted to use a `uintptr_t` instead of `void *` just to stress the fact that this is just the address we need to free, without inadvertently accessing the field as if it's a regular void pointer. But I'll just used a void* to make it less cumbersome.
